mainTopic: Reading lists on שבת (רב ביבי vs. אביי and the high-wall case), mirrors, captions under images, and drawing lots for portions
overview: The משנה forbids reading a written list of guests and dishes on שבת. רב ביבי says this is a גזירה in case the host erases something, and אביי says it is a גזירה in case he comes to read שטרי הדיוטות (business documents). The גמרא searches for a case where the two reasons give different rulings. It tries writing high on a wall, then writing low on a wall, then writing engraved on a tablet, and each attempt is challenged. In the end it returns to the high-wall case. It answers the challenge from רבה, who forbids reading by a lamp at any height, by showing that רבה's strict view is one side of a dispute between תנאים: the first תנא forbids even high writing, while רבי אחא permits it. A parallel dispute about mirrors follows, where רבי מאיר permits a mirror fixed to the wall because a metal mirror itself could be used to cut hairs. A ברייתא then forbids reading captions under pictures on שבת, and forbids looking at idolatrous images even on weekdays, because that pushes God out of one's mind (רבי חנין). Finally, the גמרא explains that drawing lots for portions is allowed only with family, based on שמואל's rule about diners who are strict with each other, and that statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the reason for the prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה forbids reading the list of guests and dishes on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה forbids reading a written list of guests and dishes on שבת. This question sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading is not a forbidden מלאכה by itself, so the prohibition must be a rabbinic safeguard. The גמרא wants to know what that safeguard is protecting against.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that follows the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's ban on reading the list of guests and dishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason for the rabbinic ban on reading the guest list and menu on שבת.

steps.title: רב ביבי: in case he erases
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי explains that the prohibition is a גזירה so the host will not come to erase something from the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said: It is a decree in case he erases.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי gives the first answer. Reading the list was forbidden so the host will not come to erase a name or a dish from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A host checking his list might change his mind about a guest or a dish and erase it. Erasing is a forbidden מלאכה (מוחק), so חכמים forbade reading the list at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to keep people away from a real prohibition
Lest he erase (מוחק is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת)

phrases.english: Rav Beivai said:
It is a decree lest he erase.
phrases.notes: He might erase a guest or dish he regrets having listed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִמְחוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban protects against erasing from the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reason for the ban is the fear of מוחק.

steps.title: אביי: in case he reads business documents
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the prohibition is a גזירה so one will not come to read ordinary business documents, which is forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a decree in case he reads ordinary business documents.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second, different answer. Reading the list was forbidden so a person will not slide into reading business papers on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guest list looks like other everyday paperwork. If reading it were allowed, a person might also read his business documents, which are forbidden on שבת. So אביי's worry is confusion between similar kinds of writing, not erasing.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary people's documents, such as business papers and contracts

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a decree lest he read ordinary (business) documents.
phrases.notes: Reading business documents is forbidden on שבת as weekday business activity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִקְרָא בְּשִׁטְרֵי הֶדְיוֹטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing reason to רב ביבי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban protects against reading שטרי הדיוטות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reason for the ban is the fear of coming to read business documents.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case the two reasons would lead to different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to a different result in practice. This sets up the search for a case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons forbid reading a regular guest list, so in the normal case they agree. The גמרא wants a case where one reason applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the נפקא מינה between רב ביבי and אביי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different rulings.

steps.title: First suggestion: writing high on a wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the difference is writing high up on a wall. For רב ביבי there is no worry, since the writing cannot be reached to erase. For אביי there is still a worry about reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when it is written on a wall and raised up. According to the one who says 'lest he erase,' we are not concerned. According to the one who says 'lest he read,' we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer: a list written high on a wall. רב ביבי would allow reading it, and אביי would forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the writing is too high to reach, nobody can erase it, so רב ביבי's worry disappears. אביי's worry is about reading, and reading high writing is still reading, so the ban stays.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא will challenge this answer right away (steps 6–7) and try other cases (a low wall, then an engraved tablet). But those fail too, and in step 15 the גמרא comes back to this same high-wall case as its final answer.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where it is written on a wall and raised up high:

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁמָּא יִמְחוֹק — לָא חָיְישִׁינַן,
phrases.english: according to the one who says 'lest he erase,' we are not concerned,
phrases.notes: He cannot reach the writing to erase it.

phrases.english: and according to the one who says 'lest he read,' we are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 with a proposed case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: High writing on a wall: allowed per רב ביבי, forbidden per אביי.

steps.title: רב ביבי should also worry about reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first suggestion: even רב ביבי should agree that reading business documents is a concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says 'lest he erase,' let him also be concerned lest he read!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 5. Why should רב ביבי ignore אביי's worry? He could hold both concerns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'erasing' is a reason does not mean 'reading documents' is not also a reason. If both worries are valid, the high-wall case would be forbidden for רב ביבי too, and there would be no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us be concerned; we should worry

phrases.english: But according to the one who says 'lest he erase,'
let us also be concerned lest he read (business documents)!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁמָּא יִמְחוֹק נֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא יִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב ביבי would permit reading high writing on a wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing stops רב ביבי from also accepting אביי's concern, so the high wall would be forbidden for both.

steps.title: Even high up, we still worry: the lamp case
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: we do worry about erasing even when the writing is high, just as a ברייתא forbids reading by lamplight, and רבה says this applies even when the lamp is extremely high.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, are we not concerned about erasing? But a ברייתא taught: One may not read by the light of a lamp. And רבה said: Even if it is two men's height high, even two ox-goads high, even ten houses one on top of the other, he may not read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger attack on step 5. It proves from a ברייתא and from רבה that height does not remove the concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading by a lamp is forbidden in case the reader tilts the lamp to get more light, which is a forbidden מלאכה. רבה says this holds even if the lamp is impossibly high, because חכמים did not make exceptions to their גזירה. So by the same logic, high writing should not remove רב ביבי's worry about erasing either.

keyTerms.meaning: By the light of a lamp

steps.confusionAlert: The lamp is forbidden because of a fear of tilting it, not because of erasing. The גמרא brings it only to show the principle that height does not cancel a rabbinic גזירה.

phrases.english: And furthermore, are we really not concerned lest he erase?
But was it not taught: One may not read by the light of a lamp.
phrases.notes: In case he tilts the lamp toward himself.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
even if it is two men's height high,
even if it is two ox-goads high,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עֲשָׂרָה בָּתִּים זֶה עַל גַּבֵּי —
phrases.english: even if it is ten houses high, one on top of the
other, he may not read.
phrases.notes: The phrase 'זה על גבי זה' got split across two lines here; this second 'זה' finishes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ לְשֶׁמָּא יִמְחוֹק לָא חָיְישִׁינַן וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to step 5's suggestion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that high writing removes רב ביבי's worry about erasing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lamp ברייתא and רבה show that a גזירה applies even when the forbidden act seems physically impossible, so height should not matter here either.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: לא יקרא לאור הנר; רבה: even ten houses high.

steps.title: Second suggestion: writing low on a wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retracts and gives the opposite case: writing low on a wall. רב ביבי forbids reading it, since it is easy to erase. אביי permits it, because a wall will not be confused with a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is a difference between them when it is written on a wall low down. According to the one who says 'lest he erase,' we are concerned. According to the one who says 'lest he read,' we are not concerned, because a wall is not confused with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the high-wall case and replaces it with a low-wall case. Here רב ביבי forbids reading the writing and אביי allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Low writing is easy to reach and erase, so רב ביבי's worry fully applies. אביי's worry depends on confusing the list with business documents, and nobody mixes up a wall with a paper document. This also answers step 6: for רב ביבי the wall raises no concern about reading documents at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not confused or mistaken for

steps.whatToRemember: רב ביבי: the ban exists in case one erases. אביי: the ban exists in case one reads business documents. The low-wall case is only a temporary suggestion. The next step challenges it, and in step 15 the גמרא settles on writing HIGH on a wall as the difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a גזירה is shaped by its exact reason. A גזירה ignores how likely the forbidden act is (the lamp case), but it does depend on whether the feared confusion can happen at all.

phrases.english: Rather, there is a difference between them
where it is written on a wall and low down:
according to the one who says 'lest he erase,' we are concerned,
phrases.notes: The writing is within easy reach.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁמָּא יִקְרָא — לָא חָיְישִׁינַן,
phrases.english: according to the one who says 'lest he read,' we are not concerned,
since a wall is not confused with a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דִּכְתִיב אַכּוֹתֶל וּמִיתַּתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retracts step 5 in light of the challenges in steps 6 and 7 and gives a new practical difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and replacement of the proposed נפקא מינה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was writing high on a wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is writing low on a wall: erasing is possible, but confusion with documents is not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Provisional only: low wall writing would be forbidden according to רב ביבי and permitted according to אביי. Step 9 rejects this, and step 15 returns to the high-wall case.

steps.title: Challenge to the low-wall answer: the reading view should also worry about erasing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 8. אביי, who worries about reading, should also worry about erasing low writing that is easy to reach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says the worry is that he might read, let him also worry that he might erase!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8. It says that even אביי should forbid reading low writing on a wall, because someone could erase it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said אביי permits low wall-writing because a wall is not confused with a business document. But low writing is easy to reach and erase. Why would אביי ignore a worry that is plainly there? If he also forbids, the two views no longer differ in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest he read (business documents on שבת), which is אביי's reason
Lest he erase, which is רב ביבי's reason
Let him be concerned / he should worry

phrases.english: And according to the one who says 'lest he read,'
phrases.notes: אביי

phrases.english: let him also be concerned lest he erase!
phrases.notes: Low writing is easy to erase.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁמָּא יִקְרָא, לֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא יִמְחוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the low-wall answer given in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אביי permits reading low writing on a wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Low writing can easily be erased, so אביי should not ignore the erasing concern. Then there is no difference between the views.

steps.title: New answer: engraved writing on a tablet or board
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a new case where the views differ: writing carved into a tablet or board. It cannot be erased, but it might still be confused with a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is writing engraved on a tablet or a board. According to the one who says 'lest he erase,' we are not concerned. According to the one who says 'lest he read,' we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the low-wall case and offers a new example. Carved writing on a tablet cannot be erased, so רב ביבי permits it. אביי still forbids it, because reading it is like reading a document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Engraving removes the erasing worry completely, since there is no ink to rub off. A tablet, however, looks like something people write documents on, so the reading worry remains. This seems like a clean case where the two reasons split.

keyTerms.meaning: Engraved, carved into the surface (not written in ink)
There is a practical difference between them

phrases.english: Rather, there is a difference between them
phrases.notes: Introduces a new case.

phrases.english: where it is engraved on a tablet or on a board:

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁמָּא יִמְחוֹק — לָא חָיְישִׁינַן,
phrases.english: according to the one who says 'lest he erase,' we are not concerned,
phrases.notes: Carved writing cannot be erased.

phrases.english: according to the one who says 'lest he read,' we are concerned.
phrases.notes: It can still lead to reading documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דַּחֲיִיק אַטַּבְלָא וְאַפִּינְקָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the low-wall case after the challenge in Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was low writing on a wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is engraved writing on a tablet: רב ביבי permits it, אביי forbids it.

steps.title: Challenge: the erasing view should also worry about reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 10. רב ביבי should also worry about reading when the writing is on a tablet.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says 'lest he erase,' let him also be concerned lest he read!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the tablet answer. Even רב ביבי should forbid a tablet, because a tablet can be confused with a business document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ביבי's main worry is erasing, but that does not mean he ignores other real worries. If a tablet really looks like a document, he too should forbid it. Then the views would agree, and Step 10 would fail.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: And according to the one who says 'lest he erase,'
phrases.notes: רב ביבי

phrases.english: let him also be concerned lest he read!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁמָּא יִמְחוֹק, לֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא יִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the engraved-tablet answer of Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב ביבי permits engraved writing on a tablet.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reading worry applies to a tablet, so רב ביבי should also forbid it. Then the views do not differ.

steps.title: Blocking the escape: a ברייתא treats tablets differently from walls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible defense that a tablet is not confused with a document. It quotes a ברייתא that permits reading a guest list from a wall but not from a tablet or board.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that a tablet or board is not confused with a document, but it was taught: A person may count how many guests are inside, how many are outside, and how many portions he will serve them from writing on a wall, but not from writing on a tablet or board!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects someone to answer, "A tablet is not like a document," and rejects that answer in advance. It cites a ברייתא that forbids reading from a tablet even though it allows reading from a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws a line between a wall and a tablet. That suggests a tablet is like a document in a way a wall is not. The גמרא will now prove that the ברייתא is talking about engraved writing.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא heads off a possible answer)

phrases.english: And if you will say:
a tablet or board is not confused with a document —
but wasn't it taught: a person may count how many are inside
and how many are outside
and how many portions he will place before them
from writing that is on the wall,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מִכְּתָב שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי טַבְלָא וּפִינְקָס!
phrases.english: but not from writing that is on a tablet or board!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: טַבְלָא וּפִינְקָס בִּשְׁטָרָא לָא מִיחַלַּף — וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of Step 11 by blocking a defense.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense of רב ביבי: that a tablet is not confused with a document.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids a tablet but permits a wall, which shows a tablet is treated like a document.

steps.title: What case is the ברייתא talking about? Ink writing does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of writing the ברייתא means. If it means ink, there would be no reason to separate a wall from a tablet.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it was written in ink, what is the difference between here and here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its proof by asking what case the ברייתא describes. It rules out writing in ink first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ink can be erased from a wall just as easily as from a tablet. So if the ברייתא meant ink, the erasing worry would apply to both, and there would be no reason to treat them differently. Ink therefore cannot be the case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (the first option, about to be rejected)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say it was actually written (in ink) —

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא.
phrases.english: what is the difference here, and what is the difference here?
phrases.notes: Wall vs. tablet would be the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in Step 12 to build the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ברייתא talking about ink writing or engraved writing?

steps.title: The ברייתא must mean engraved writing, so the tablet is forbidden because of reading
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be talking about engraved writing. Even so, it forbids a tablet, so the worry must be reading, and that would apply to רב ביבי too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not a case where it is engraved, and it teaches: from writing on the wall, but not from writing on a tablet or board!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. The ברייתא is about engraved writing, and it still forbids a tablet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Engraved writing cannot be erased, so the only reason left to forbid a tablet is that it gets confused with a document. That reading worry should apply for רב ביבי as well. The tablet answer from Step 10 therefore collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not? (introduces the only option left)

steps.whatToRemember: Engraved writing on a tablet is forbidden only because of the reading worry. So the tablet case cannot be where רב ביבי and אביי disagree.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that it is engraved, and it teaches:
from writing that is on the wall

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מִכְּתָב שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי טַבְלָא וּפִינְקָס!
phrases.english: but not from writing that is on a tablet or board!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Steps 12 and 13, which knocks out Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That a tablet is confused with a document, so רב ביבי would also forbid engraved tablets.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of counting guests, read as describing engraved writing.

steps.title: Back to the first answer: high writing on a wall, and רבה's view is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the first suggestion: the views differ about writing high on a wall. It answers the challenge from רבה by saying that רבה's view matches only one side of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: really, it is written on a wall and is high up. And what was difficult for you from רבה, רבה's view is a matter of dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its original idea from Step 5. It then explains why the challenge from רבה in Step 7 does not disprove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 used רבה, who forbids reading by a lamp even when it is very high, to show that height does not help. The גמרא answers that רבה's view is just one opinion in a dispute among תנאים. רב ביבי can follow the other opinion, which is not worried about high writing.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (returns to an earlier idea)
It is a dispute between תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new case. It is the same high-wall case from Step 5, now defended against the challenge from רבה.

phrases.english: Rather: really, it is written on a wall and is raised high,
and as for what was difficult for you from רבה —
רבה's view is a dispute between תנאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the tablet answer fails, the גמרא returns to the answer from Step 5 and answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Return to an earlier answer (לעולם); the challenge is shown to depend on one side of a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's ruling proves that height never removes the worry, so the high-wall case fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה matches only one תנא. רב ביבי can follow the other view, so high writing on a wall is a real difference between the views.

steps.title: Source for the dispute: the first תנא and רבי אחא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute. The first תנא forbids counting guests from any writing, and רבי אחא permits it from writing on a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: A person may count his guests and his appetizers from memory, but not from writing. רבי אחא permits from writing that is on a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows the dispute between תנאים mentioned in Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא forbids all written lists, which fits the strict approach of רבה. רבי אחא permits writing on a wall, which shows there is a תנא who is not worried in that case. This gives רב ביבי a תנא to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: From his mouth, meaning from memory

steps.whatToRemember: The high-wall case stands as the difference between רב ביבי and אביי. רבה's strict view is only one side of a dispute between תנאים, and רבי אחא permits writing on a wall.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא: when an אמורא's ruling is used as a challenge, the גמרא can answer that the ruling follows only one תנא, so another view is still possible.

phrases.english: As it was taught: a person may count his guests
and his appetizers from memory,
but not from writing.
רבי אחא permits
from writing that is on the wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מוֹנֶה אָדָם אֶת אוֹרְחָיו וְאֶת פַּרְפְּרוֹתָיו מִפִּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the dispute between תנאים claimed in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That רבה's strict view is disputed by another תנא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the first תנא (forbids all writing) and רבי אחא (permits writing on a wall).

steps.title: What case does רבי אחא permit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of wall writing רבי אחא allows. It rules out writing low on the wall, because there we would worry that a person might erase it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it is written low down on the wall, we should worry that a person might erase it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exact case רבי אחא is talking about. It rejects the first option, writing low on the wall, and sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing low on the wall is within easy reach, so a person might erase it on שבת. רבי אחא would not permit that case. This leaves only writing high on the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
If you say (the first option, about to be rejected)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: This asks about רבי אחא's lenient ruling from the previous ברייתא.

phrases.english: If you say that it is written low down —
we should be concerned that perhaps he will erase it!
phrases.notes: Erasing writing is forbidden on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This defines the case of רבי אחא's ruling from the ברייתא in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where on the wall is the writing that רבי אחא permits reading?

steps.title: רבה's view is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The writing must be high on the wall. So the first תנא, who forbids even high writing, matches רבה, and רבי אחא disagrees. רבה's view is therefore one side of a dispute between תנאים. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not about writing that is high up? Learn from this that רבה's view is a dispute between תנאים. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי אחא permits only writing high on the wall. This means רבה's view is one side of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing high on the wall cannot easily be erased, yet the first תנא still forbids it, just as רבה forbids a lamp even when it is very high. רבי אחא permits high writing. So רבה follows the first תנא, and רב ביבי can follow רבי אחא. This answers the challenge from רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (introduces the only remaining option)
It is a dispute between תנאים
Learn from it (here, the final acceptance)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אחא permits reading only writing that is high on a wall, where erasing is not a concern. The first תנא forbids even that. רבה's strict view matches the first תנא, so it is one side of a dispute between תנאים, and רב ביבי can follow רבי אחא. The high-wall case therefore stands as the difference between רב ביבי and אביי.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase שמע מינה appears twice here. The first time, it is part of the proposal ("and learn from this that..."). The second time, standing alone, the גמרא is agreeing: "Yes, learn from it."

phrases.english: Rather, is it not where it is written and raised high,
and learn from this that the view of Rabba is a dispute of tannaim?
Indeed, learn from it.
phrases.notes: The גמרא accepts the conclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 17 ruled out writing low on the wall, so this step concludes that the case is writing high on the wall.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה's strict rule (height does not remove the concern) is one side of a dispute between תנאים. The first תנא forbids even high writing, as רבה would, while רבי אחא permits it. So רב ביבי can permit high wall writing, and that is the difference between him and אביי.

steps.title: A parallel dispute about mirrors on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this dispute matches another dispute between תנאים. The first תנא forbids looking in a mirror on שבת. רבי מאיר permits looking in a mirror fixed to the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: These תנאים are like those תנאים. As it was taught: one may not look in a mirror on שבת. רבי מאיר permits it with a mirror fixed to the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar dispute about mirrors on שבת. This sets up the next step, which will look closely at רבי מאיר's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with a mirror is that a person will see a stray hair and remove it on שבת. The first תנא forbids every mirror, just as he forbade all reading. רבי מאיר makes an exception for a mirror fixed to the wall, much like רבי אחא made an exception for writing on the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: These תנאים are like those תנאים (the two disputes run parallel)

phrases.english: And these tannaim are like those tannaim.
phrases.notes: The first תנא matches the strict view, and רבי מאיר matches רבי אחא.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One may not look in a mirror on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: The worry is that he will see a hanging hair and remove it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir permits
in a mirror that is fixed on the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This compares the dispute settled in step 18 to a parallel dispute about mirrors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first תנא forbids looking in any mirror on שבת. רבי מאיר permits looking in a mirror fixed to the wall.

steps.title: Why should a fixed mirror be different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר. If a fixed mirror is allowed because he will remember it is שבת while going to get scissors, the same should be true for a mirror that is not fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a mirror fixed to the wall? Is it that in the meantime he will remember? With one that is not fixed, too, in the meantime he will remember!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי מאיר's distinction between a fixed mirror and a loose one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A possible reason for רבי מאיר's leniency is that a person must walk away to get scissors, and on the way he will remember it is שבת. But he would also need scissors with a loose mirror. So this reason does not explain why only a fixed mirror is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile; in the time in between

phrases.english: What is different about one fixed on the wall —
that in the meantime he remembers?
phrases.notes: While going to get scissors, he will remember it is שבת.

phrases.english: With one that is not fixed, too:
in the meantime he remembers!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the reason behind רבי מאיר's ruling in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's distinction between a mirror fixed to the wall and one that is not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The "he will remember while getting scissors" reason applies equally to both mirrors, so it cannot be what separates them.

steps.title: The case is a metal mirror
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a metal mirror. It follows the teaching of רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a metal mirror, and it follows רב נחמן's statement in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא to a metal mirror. It then sets up a quote from רב נחמן to explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is no longer about fetching scissors. The new worry comes from the metal mirror itself. The next step gives the source for this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with (narrows the case)
And it is like the teaching of רב נחמן

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a metal mirror,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ.
phrases.english: and it is like Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a metal mirror
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry is that he will go to get scissors, and that worry is the same for every mirror.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry is that he will use the metal mirror itself to cut, and that does not apply when the mirror is fixed to the wall.

steps.title: Why a metal mirror is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, explains that a metal mirror is forbidden because a person may use it to cut off hanging hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Why did they say a metal mirror is forbidden? Because a person tends to remove hanging hairs with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source behind its answer. A metal mirror can itself be used to cut stray hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the mirror itself can cut, the person does not need to walk away for scissors, so "he will remember" does not help. A mirror fixed to the wall cannot be used this way, so רבי מאיר permits it. This matches רבי אחא's view: writing high on a wall is permitted because it is hard to erase.

keyTerms.meaning: For what reason did they say?

steps.whatToRemember: Both disputes follow the same pattern. The strict תנא forbids everything. The lenient תנא (רבי אחא or רבי מאיר) permits something fixed to the wall, because the feared action (erasing or cutting) cannot easily be done with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the two disputes rest on the same idea. A rabbinic worry can disappear when the object is fixed to a wall, because the forbidden act becomes impractical.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: For Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
For what reason did they say
that a metal mirror is forbidden —
because a person tends to remove with it
phrases.notes: He uses the mirror's sharp edge itself to cut.

phrases.english: hanging hairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the source for the metal-mirror answer in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That the worry with a metal mirror is cutting hairs with the mirror itself
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה

steps.title: Writing under a picture may not be read on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that writing placed under a picture or image may not be read on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים taught: writing that runs under a picture or under images may not be read on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds another case to the rules about reading on שבת: captions written under pictures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This caption counts as everyday, non-holy writing, like the guest lists discussed earlier. The concern is the same one as before: reading ordinary writing on שבת may lead a person to read business documents (שטרי הדיוטות).

keyTerms.meaning: Images or portraits, often of people or idols

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Writing that runs under a picture
phrases.notes: A caption explaining the picture

phrases.english: and under images —
it is forbidden to read it on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: A rabbinic safeguard against reading business documents

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of which kinds of writing may be read on שבת, after the mirror digression.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Captions under pictures or images may not be read on שבת.

steps.title: Looking at an idolatrous image is forbidden even on weekdays
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds that the image itself may not be looked at even on a weekday, based on the פסוק "אל תפנו אל האלילים".
steps.simpleTranslation: And the image itself may not be looked at even on a weekday, because the פסוק says: "Do not turn to the idols."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues: the caption is only a שבת problem, but the image itself is a problem every day of the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules come from different sources. The caption ban is a rabbinic rule about שבת. Looking at the idolatrous image is banned at all times because of a פסוק in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: On a weekday (not שבת or יום טוב)
To gaze at or look at

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. Reading the caption is forbidden only on שבת. Looking at the image is forbidden every day, and the reason has nothing to do with שבת.

phrases.english: And the image itself —
even on a weekday it is forbidden to look at it,
because it is said:
"Do not turn to the idols."
phrases.notes: ויקרא יט:ד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second clause of the same ברייתא, which raises the image itself to a year-round ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Looking at an idolatrous image is forbidden even on weekdays, based on "אל תפנו אל האלילים".

steps.title: How does the verse teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק shows that merely looking is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the derivation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the words of the פסוק teach a ban on looking. It is setting up רבי חנין's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Do not turn to idols" sounds like it is about worshipping them. The גמרא wants to know where in these words a ban on just looking can be found.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the derivation? How is this learned from the פסוק?

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the פסוק quoted in step 24 supports the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How "אל תפנו אל האלילים" teaches a ban on merely looking at images.

steps.title: Do not push God out of your mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין rereads the פסוק as "אל תְּפַנּוּ אֵל": do not clear God out of your thoughts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said: Do not clear God out of your mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנין answers by reading the words of the פסוק in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads "תִּפְנוּ" (turn) as "תְּפַנּוּ" (empty out), and "אֶל" (to) as "אֵל" (God). Staring at an idol fills your mind with it and pushes out the awareness of God. That is why even looking is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Captions under pictures may not be read on שבת. Idolatrous images may never be looked at, because looking at them pushes God out of a person's mind (רבי חנין).

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said:
Do not clear God out of your mind.
phrases.notes: A wordplay reading of "אל תפנו אל"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is read as "do not empty God from your mind". Gazing at idols does exactly that.

steps.title: Drawing lots allowed with family, not with others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה allowing a person to draw lots with his children and infers that this is not allowed with outsiders.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A person may draw lots with his children," and so on. With his children and household, yes. With someone else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about drawing lots for portions at the שבת table. It points out an implied limit: this is allowed only with family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says "with his children". From this the גמרא learns that drawing lots with an outsider is not allowed. This inference sets up the question of why the difference exists.

phrases.english: A person may draw lots with his children, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה

phrases.aramaic: עִם בָּנָיו וְעִם בְּנֵי בֵיתוֹ אִין,
phrases.english: With his children and household members, yes;
but with another person, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawing lots for portions on שבת is allowed only with one's family, not with outsiders.

steps.title: Why not with outsiders?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why drawing lots with outsiders is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the limit it just found. It is setting up the answer from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act is the same in both cases, so it is not obvious why the people involved should matter. The גמרא needs a reason that separates family from outsiders.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the inference in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why drawing lots on שבת is allowed with family but not with others.

steps.title: Group members who are strict with each other violate measuring rules
steps.stepSummary: The reason follows רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: diners who are strict about exact shares violate the bans on measuring, weighing, counting, and lending and repaying on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רב יהודה, who said in the name of שמואל: members of a group who are strict with each other about their shares violate the bans on measuring, weighing, and counting, and the ban on lending and repaying on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with שמואל's teaching. Outsiders care about exact portions, and that turns the meal into a business-like transaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Family members do not care who gets slightly more, so drawing lots is just friendly fun. People who are strict with each other are really measuring and settling accounts, like a business deal, and that is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב. Since outsiders are usually particular, drawing lots with them is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Members of a group eating together
Who are strict or particular about exact shares

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key test: what matters is whether the people are strict with each other, not the act of drawing lots itself.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel.
For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה הַמַּקְפִּידִין זֶה עַל זֶה —
phrases.english: Members of a group who are strict with one another —
violate the ban on measuring,
and the bans on weighing and counting,
and the ban on borrowing and repaying on a Festival,
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 with an outside statement by an אמורא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Outsiders are particular about exact shares, so drawing lots with them amounts to forbidden measuring and business-like settling of accounts.
